title: Founder Access is revoked permanently the moment the Transformation Primitive is Invoked
content:
A.2.2.1.1.3.2 defines "Founder Access" as the ability to freely edit the Scaffold Artifact, including Activating any desired Primitives and adding custom Omni Documents — and then sets its expiry: it "is revoked at the moment the Founder Invokes either the Prime Transformation or Executor Transformation Primitive." A.2.2.1.1.8 confirms the freeze, and A.2.2.1.2.4.1.1 confirms that during the pre-Transformation stage the Founder holds "unilateral authority" with "no Operational Executor Facilitator approval or token holder vote required."

The structure is a **one-way trade**. Before Transformation, the Founder has total control but no recognized status; Transformation buys recognition as a Prime or Executor Agent at the price of that control, permanently. Afterwards the Founder "cannot add or edit Omni Documents, but can only Activate and Invoke specific Primitives so that the Agent can complete setup," and A.2.2.1.2.4.1.2 fixes even the order: Agent Token, then Executor Accord, then Root Edit.

This is what makes the Agent's constitution credible. Anything genuinely custom about an Agent — its Omni Documents, its bespoke rules — must be committed *before* the Agent can claim ecosystem status, and is thereafter amendable only through token holder vote (A.2.2.1.1.15). A Founder cannot raise capital under one constitution and then quietly rewrite it.

The cost is that the pre-Transformation window is the only chance to get custom structure right, and it is exercised when the Agent has the least information and no token holders to check it.
description: Unilateral editing power is exchanged for recognized Agent status; afterwards the Founder can only Invoke a fixed sequence of Primitives and can never edit Omni Documents again.
